messages.subject: Repost: Changing Bar Widths for Barcharts with Categorical x-axis  Variables
parts:
ggplot2 group:

Reposted with better formatting, and a correction:

I would like to control the width of the bars in a categorical
stacked barchart. I thought this might be possible with
position_stack but I cannot see how to do this from the
documentation.

Here is a reproducible example:

a <- data.frame(type=c(rep(c("A", "B", "C"), 4)),
variable=c(sort(rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), 3))),
value = c(30, 20, 50, 20, 40, 40,
10, 80, 10, 5, 20, 75))
p <-ggplot(a, aes(x=factor(variable), y=value,
fill = type)) + geom_bar()
p

I would like to leave more white space between the bars.

Paul

messages.author: 0f7afe3850f58838
messages.subject: Re: Repost: Changing Bar Widths for Barcharts with Categorical x-axis  Variables
parts:
After continued trial and error, I discovered that a simple:
+ geom_bar(width=0.5) makes categorical bars that
are 1/2 width, etc.

This is an undocumented feature, as a search of the
page: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html for the
word "width" revealed no hits.

It appears that position_stack is used automatically
when x is a categorical variable.

I believe it might be clearer if the documentation for
position_stack mentioned this, or contained an
example that used one of the parameters of
position_stack:
position_stack(width=NULL, height=NULL, ...)

As written, the page only has an example for
binwidth= . In addition, for a ggplot2 newbie,
the default, within parens after position_stack
is somewhat confusing when the "width"
argument is actually added to geom_bar(),
not position_stack().

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Repost: Changing Bar Widths for Barcharts with Categorical x-axis  Variables
parts:
> After continued trial and error, I discovered that a simple:
> + geom_bar(width=0.5) makes categorical bars that
> are 1/2 width, etc.

> This is an undocumented feature, as a search of the
> page: http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_bar.html for the
> word "width" revealed no hits.

It's undocumented because width is a bit of strange creature - it's
sort of an aesthetic, but it isn't transformed by any scale and only
really makes sense in cartesian coordinates. I'm not completely sure
how to document it.

> It appears that position_stack is used automatically
> when x is a categorical variable.

Position stack is always used with geom_bar (unless otherwise
specified), but it doesn't have any relevance to your problem - the
width there is a red herring, and only exists for compatibility with
the other positions which do actually use it.

Hadley
